Text: $CBRS Cerebras uses a Weight Streaming architecture. The entire model does not need to sit in SRAM simultaneously; weights are streamed onto the wafer layer-by-layer from external memory (like DDR5 or HBM) right as they are needed for computation. This masks memory latency behind the compute time, meaning you do not need $100M+ of wafers just to host a model like Qwen3-235B.

Text: $CBRS for KV CACHE : Groq’s Bottleneck: Because a single Groq chip only holds around 230–500 MB of SRAM, a 70B model requires hundreds of networked Groq chips just to store the weights. The exploding KV cache must then be partitioned and distributed over this complex network of chips, creating severe communication and compiling overhead as context windows grow.Cerebras’s Solution: Cerebras features a massive, single Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE-3) containing 44 GB of SRAM on one continuous piece of silicon. This allows entire layers of frontier models—along with massive multi-turn context windows—to stay completely intact on a single wafer. Activations and KV caches do not have to pay a "network tax" to move across external wires.

Text: $CBRS Moving your AI workloads from NVIDIA to Cerebras hardware today is no longer a brutal or manual process, but it does come with specific structural constraints that developers must keep in mind. Cerebras has built a seamless software bridge to combat NVIDIA’s CUDA monopoly, making standard migrations surprisingly easy. However, because a Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine (like the CS-3 or CS-4) compiles an entire neural network as a single physical graph rather than distributing it across separate chips, the underlying software behavior differs from a traditional GPU cluster. What Makes It Easy • Native PyTorch Integration: You do not have to rewrite your entire codebase or learn a completely new raw assembly language. Through the Cerebras Software Platform (CSoft) and the open-source cerebras-pytorch package, you wrap your existing PyTorch models in Cerebras runner classes.

Text: $CBRS Cerebras lockup expiration is unusual: How the Staggered Lockup Works • Day 1 and Day 2: Cerebras Systems released 2.5 million employee shares immediately, with another 2.5 million unlocking on day two because the stock closed above 133% of its IPO price. • Post-Earnings Waves: Tranches of 27.7 million shares and 36.4 million shares unlocked two trading days after the first-quarter and second-quarter earnings reports on June 23 and August 12. • Biweekly Tranches: Intermediate releases of about 14.6 million shares each occurred on August 19, September 2, and September 16. • Upcoming Scheduled Waves: Three additional tranches of roughly 19.4 million shares each land on September 30, October 14, and October 28. • The Final Expiry: All remaining locked shares become eligible for sale on November 9, 2026 (the standard 180-day mark) or two trading days after third-quarter earnings, whichever comes first.
